Since another is named as AsyncFileLogger, should this be named as SyncFileLogger for clarity?
Done

Just curious why mutex should be part of interface? 
Thread safety should be offered by class actually implementing the write if required? Interface should keep things flexible such that it can be extended where thread safety is not required?

Both the derived classes `SyncFileLogger` and `AsyncFileLogger` are using the `mutex` to make file logging multi-thread safe. Hence this member has been kept in the interface. I do not see any harm in keeping it in the interface.

>Interface should keep things flexible such that it can be extended where thread safety is not required?

If the derived class does not require multi thread safety, it can not use the mutex.

Its not about harm, its about the design usability. 
Why should an interface mandate a mutex variable?
As discussed, removed mutex from interface.
Why a synchronous logging needs mutex handling? We won't be using it with threads.

Synchronous logging and multi-thread safety are mutually exclusive. Synchronous logging means the `logMessage()` is blocking. 

>We won't be using it with threads.

Yes, currently we plan to use this for logging VPD write actions, which are expected to be from a single thread, but there is not much additional cost in ensuring this API is multi-thread safe.

Even if there is no cost, why should we have a mutex blocking in this case?

These are kind of hidden classes(since the construction is controlled and limited only to friend classes). Reason of having that is to cater very specific requirements.
Currently I don't see a use case as per our requirement. Can be extended in case any such requirement pops up in future?
As discussed, removed `mutex` from `SyncFileLogger`, update doxygen to reflect that this class is not multi-thread safe.

Who will handle this? The caller trying to log?
In case of exception, just log to console? Anyways caller if handles the exception will have to so the same.
Agree with this. Will update this to log to console in case of exception caught.
Done
